statusDetail: Atomic coverage complete. The external web and image result backends returned failure/empty states during the run; those observed states are reported as findings rather than blockers because the templates remained inspectable.

page.framework: server-rendered Yahoo Search templates with client-side enhancements
page.notes: Representative coverage: landing, web-result error state, image-result empty/error state, and linked sign-in entry. Video/news modes were excluded because they share the inspected result shell and live data was unavailable; authenticated account completion and destructive/report flows were not exercised.

paths.description: Public search landing: primary query form, trends, preferences, mobile/reduced-motion/forced-colors, load performance, network, security, no-JS, and memory.
Primary web-search journey and failure recovery; represents the general web results template.
Image search mode and no-results recovery; represents the media-result navigation shell.
Linked sign-in entry inspected for account-flow clarity, autofill, and modern authentication support. Credential submission was intentionally not performed.

findings.summary: The search experience ignores the user’s dark color-scheme preference.
findings.evidence: The dark-mode screenshot is pixel-identical in surface treatment to the light screenshot, and the CSS probe found no color-scheme, prefers-color-scheme, or light-dark() support.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme: light dark and define preference-driven surface, text, control, and icon colors with prefers-color-scheme or light-dark().

findings.summary: Search navigation swaps abruptly instead of preserving spatial continuity.
findings.evidence: The recorded query submission changes from landing to results without a View Transition; the CSS probe found no view-transition usage.
findings.suggestedFix: Use same-document or cross-document View Transitions for search submission and result-mode changes, with a reduced-motion fallback.

findings.summary: The apps menu is not implemented as an anchored, self-repositioning overlay.
findings.evidence: The overlay probe identifies an anchor-like <a role=button> and a plain #yucs-apps-overlay <div> with no popover or anchor positioning; the CSS probe found no anchor-name/position-anchor rules.
findings.suggestedFix: Use popover plus CSS anchor positioning and position-try fallbacks so the menu stays attached and avoids viewport edges.

findings.summary: Transient menu UI uses an ad-hoc div instead of the platform popover primitive.
findings.evidence: Across the inspected DOM there are zero popover, dialog, or details elements; #yucs-apps-overlay is a role-less div.
findings.suggestedFix: Implement the transient apps menu with popover and declarative light-dismiss, retaining accessible expanded state on its trigger.

findings.summary: The primary search and result templates do not reflow for a 360px viewport.
findings.evidence: The landing has no viewport meta and renders a 980px CSS canvas scaled down; web results overflow by 920px and image results by 441px. Screenshots show tiny landing content and clipped result copy/navigation.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a correct viewport meta to every template, replace fixed-width shells with intrinsic fluid layout, and test all search modes at narrow widths without horizontal overflow.

findings.summary: Shared result components do not adapt to their available container.
findings.evidence: The CSS probes found no container-query support, while both result archetypes retain wide desktop rows and overflow their 360px visual viewport.
findings.suggestedFix: Give reusable result/nav components containment and use size-aware container queries for compact layouts, with an intrinsic fallback.

findings.summary: The core search task could not return web or image results.
findings.evidence: A recorded web query ends at “We had temporary problems searching for web pages”; the image route says no results for a broad query. Both primary result archetypes failed during this run.
findings.suggestedFix: Restore and monitor the search backend path, preserve the query across retry, and provide a reliable fallback/result source before considering secondary UX work.

findings.summary: Throttled mobile loading misses the LCP good range.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured LCP at 9.8s, Time to Interactive at 9.8s, and performance 0.70. The unthrottled trace was much faster (LCP 1.28s), so the risk is strongest under constrained mobile conditions.
findings.suggestedFix: Profile the Lighthouse LCP dependency chain, prioritize the LCP element, and defer consent/analytics and nonessential media until after primary content.

findings.summary: The sparse landing page transfers 1.36MB, including 505KB of voice audio before the feature is used.
findings.evidence: The HAR summary records 27 requests and 1,363,282 transferred bytes: 505,543 media bytes and 693,869 script bytes. Four voice WAV files are among the largest requests.
findings.suggestedFix: Fetch voice assets only after voice-search intent, compress/modernize audio where possible, and shorten the critical dependency chain.

findings.summary: Large portions of consent, analytics, and mobile CSS are unused at load.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse estimates 409KiB unused JavaScript and 39KiB unused CSS; major waste comes from Didomi and Google Tag Manager bundles.
findings.suggestedFix: Split and conditionally load consent UI and analytics, remove duplicate/unused styles, and load only the code needed for the initial search surface.

findings.summary: Some primary controls lack accessible names.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse accessibility is 0.82 and identifies the apps and mail links as unnamed in the mobile variant. The web-results search text field also has no label in the DOM probe.
findings.suggestedFix: Give every icon link and search input a stable accessible name; avoid empty aria-label values across responsive variants.

findings.summary: The landing page lacks a main landmark and starts its visible heading hierarchy at h3.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reports no main landmark and a non-sequential heading order; the DOM probe lists h3 followed by h4 items and no h1/h2.
findings.suggestedFix: Wrap primary content in <main> and use a logical h1/h2 hierarchy while preserving the visible design.

findings.summary: Mobile scaling and clipping make text difficult to read.
findings.evidence: At 360px, the landing is scaled to fit a 980px layout and result copy extends outside the viewport; the screenshots show tiny text or truncated recovery instructions.
findings.suggestedFix: Use responsive typography and intrinsic layout so text remains comfortably sized and reflows without clipping at mobile and zoomed conditions.

findings.summary: The page logs a failed network resource to the browser console.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse records a 404 from https://acapi.yahoo.com/v1/sync?... during load.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove the stale request or handle the integration without emitting a failed network error; add monitoring for repeated client-side resource failures.

findings.summary: Result templates omit a meta description.
findings.evidence: Both web and image result probes report description: null. Lighthouse’s mobile landing variant also reports no meta description, despite the desktop variant including one.
findings.suggestedFix: Emit a stable, query-aware meta description server-side on every public template and keep metadata consistent across responsive/UA variants.

findings.summary: Cookie and CSP settings weaken an otherwise HTTPS-protected page.
findings.evidence: HTTPS, HSTS, nosniff and frame protection are present, but CSP allows unsafe-inline and unsafe-eval. Cookies sBS and _dmit lack Secure; several cookies use SameSite=None.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove unsafe-eval/unsafe-inline through nonces/hashes and set Secure plus the narrowest viable SameSite policy on every cookie.

findings.summary: Third-party delivery and tracking dominate the landing load.
findings.evidence: The HAR attributes 22 of 27 requests and 1,316,474 of 1,363,282 transferred bytes to third-party origins; the tracker probe finds Google Tag Manager.
findings.suggestedFix: Minimise telemetry, self-host or remove nonessential dependencies, batch necessary analytics, and load them only after an appropriate legal/user signal.

findings.summary: The linked sign-in flow does not expose phishing-resistant passkey authentication.
findings.evidence: The sign-in screenshot offers username and Google sign-in; the probe finds no passkey text or WebAuthn/navigator.credentials integration. Permission prompts are not requested on search load.
findings.suggestedFix: Offer passkey/WebAuthn registration and authentication as a first-class sign-in option, while retaining recovery and federated fallbacks.

findings.summary: Defensive browser policy coverage is incomplete.
findings.evidence: The header probe finds no Permissions-Policy, a permissive no-referrer-when-downgrade policy, unsafe CSP script directives, object-src *, and connect-src *.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a least-privilege Permissions-Policy and Referrer-Policy, narrow CSP sources, set object-src none, and constrain connect-src/media-src to required origins.

findings.summary: The CSS is built around physical left/right positioning rather than writing-mode-safe logical properties.
findings.evidence: html lang=en-US is correct, but the probe finds no logical-property usage and 31 physical left/right declarations on the landing; no explicit dir is provided.
findings.suggestedFix: Set direction deliberately where needed and replace physical margins, padding, inset, and alignment with inline/block logical properties.

findings.summary: The username field does not advertise the autocomplete token browsers need.
findings.evidence: The linked sign-in probe reports name=username with an empty autocomplete value, despite a visible “Username, email or phone number” label.
findings.suggestedFix: Set autocomplete=username (and use current-password or webauthn on the next step) so password managers and autofill can assist safely.

findings.summary: Nonessential scripts and audio are fetched before user intent.
findings.evidence: The initial 1.36MB load includes 505KB of voice WAV media and Lighthouse estimates 409KiB unused JavaScript on a page whose core UI is one search field.
findings.suggestedFix: Defer voice media until activation, conditionally load consent/analytics code, and set a page-weight budget tied to the sparse search task.
